title.narrative: NIHR Global Health Research Centre for Non-communicable Diseases and Environmental Change

description.narrative: The NIHR Global Health Research Centre for non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and Environmental Change will be a recognised centre of excellence on NCDs and global environmental change in low and middle-income countries (LMICs), offering world-leading research, training and policy advice for health equity within 5 years. It includes four LMIC-based institutions working in three countries, Bangladesh, India, and Indonesia. The target NCDs are hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD) and Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).The Centre addresses crucial knowledge gaps through three integrated research themes: •Strengthening primary health care and essential public health services for NCD prevention and management in communities affected by rapid environmental change; •Developing and evaluating multi-sectoral interventions that have dual benefits in reducing the burden of NCDs and hazardous environmental exposures at the population level; •Strengthening engagement of communities in the generation and use of evidence and advocacy for health and environment policy change.The Centre focusses on strengthening primary health care through establishment of a digital platform, and developing and evaluating multi-sectoral interventions addressing coastal water salinity and hypertension in Bangladesh, leveraging food aid for NCD prevention in India and reducing effects of plastics burning and air pollution in Indonesia. Community engagement and involvement activities will be key in the evidence-to-policy process in each of the research focus areas to identify opportunities for strengthening impact outcomes.Throughout the research lifecycle, the Centre emphasises systematic and meaningful engagement of community members and policymakers – including through co-design and evaluation of interventions. In addition to delivering high-quality impactful research, research capacity strengthening is a top priority. The Centre is delivering several training and development opportunities targeting three critical career periods: (1) pre-doctoral, (2) early post-doctoral and (3) transitioning to senior leadership.The Centre’s Theory of Change aims to bring positive impact through:-•Enhanced health equity, wellbeing and environmental sustainability across Asia (SDGs 3, 5, 10, 13, and 17); •Strengthened research infrastructure for generating high-quality evidence on NCDs in populations most vulnerable to environmental change; •Mobilised CEI capability to ensure evidence, advocacy and policy action is community-centric and benefits the most vulnerable.
